text:
maya: kicked off a focused long-context bench today to reproduce the memory growth we saw in prod-like runs. details below.

sam: ack — paste the exact bench invocation and the node you saw growth on?

maya: command i used:
```
bench-run --suite long-context-stress \
  --seq-length 49152 \
  --concurrency 32 \
  --duration 2h \
  --kv-reuse=true \
  --kv-cache-cap=16GB \
  --batching=continuous \
  --pattern=frag-reuse-sparse
```
node: perf-stage-ded-07
profile: infra/bench/profiles/long-heavy-sparse.yaml

maya: sample RSS timeline from that node:
```
[00:10] RSS=10.1G cached=1.4M frag=68%
[00:40] RSS=12.8G cached=1.45M frag=71%
[01:10] RSS=15.3G cached=1.45M frag=74%
[01:40] RSS=17.6G cached=1.45M frag=76%
```
pprof heap top (condensed):
```
1.5GB  kv_reuse_lookup
0.8GB  kv_fragment_scan
0.6GB  std::vector allocations
0.4GB  kernel_selector::choose_variant
```

leo: interesting — fragmentation climbs even though cached_entries barely moves. smells like tombstone metadata or slot churn not compacted. what did compact interval look like?

anika: default compaction interval is 60s in this profile. i toggled it to 15s in a quick experiment and fragmentation still trended up (only a small drop).

maya: perf top flame snippet shows heavy time in kv_reuse_lookup and fragment scan, less so in kernel selection.
```
35%  kv_reuse_lookup
22%  kv_fragment_scan
8%   memcpy
6%   kernel_selector::choose_variant
```

anika: i pushed an experimental patch that aggressively zeroes tombstone flags during slot_free and emits a lightweight compaction hint to the slot manager. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/2456

ci-bot: CI for PR #2456  bench-long-context-stress  FAILED (mem-growth threshold exceeded). artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/99821

sam: we should add a deterministic regression harness that reproduces the churn pattern — alternate long-prefix writes with scattered small updates so we exercise both reuse and fragmentation. leo can you add a synthetic test under infra/bench/tests/frag-reuse-synthetic?

leo: yes, i'll add a deterministic generator that emits sequences: write prefix N tokens, then sparse writes at random offsets, then read-heavy tails to exercise reuse. will wire it into the nightly long-context suite.

maya: queued a 24h run with the patch enabled on perf-stage-ded-07 starting 2026-03-20T01:00Z. uploaded full heap profiles and flamegraphs to artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/pprof/1998123456

anika: running experiments with batching=continuous vs batching=fixed-window to see if batching heuristics amplify working set growth. also testing kernel_selector opts to prefer compact-friendly kernels on long-seq paths.

sam: assign owners: leo -> implement regression harness; anika -> iterate on tombstone/compaction patch and run experiments; maya -> manage long runs + collect traces. @ci-bot please re-run failing bench with retain-artifacts=1.

ci-bot: re-run queued (run id 99822). will attach artifacts when complete.

maya: note for follow-ups: add perf regression criteria that monitors frag_pct and top kv-related heap allocations. current threshold for mem-growth is too coarse — it hides fragmentation-driven bloat.

sam: agreed. add a regression metric for frag_pct delta > 10% over baseline and a kv_reuse_lookup heap share increase > 15%.

maya: leaving the node live for now (ssh jump -> perf-stage-ded-07) if anyone wants to debug interactively. coffee and logs available.

leo: thanks — i'll push the synthetic harness later today and tag this thread when i have a PR.

anika: i'll iterate on PR #2456 and post perf diffs. hoping the compaction hint + tombstone zeroing reduces frag and stabilizes RSS.

maya: thanks all. keeping artifacts linked here for triage.
